The reasons the supply and demand relationship works here, is because the quantity, or market saturation of a given product or service is too high, which is to say, too many people have it. So the price goes up, to limit the number of people who have it, so that it stays at a high level, rather than inflating (think market saturation of a printed currency). The problem is, were talking about a meta,non-tangible, long lasting dynamic, namely, education.

"If every one has a degree they become pretty worthless." Are you saying that if everyone has a high school diploma that the education (amount of, ability to critically analyze and call back usefully, information) is useless?

Look, the unspoken assumption about the "value" of a college degree, as a bargaining chip in salary negotiations is just that, it is an economic armament. Fundamentally, if you view education in that way, I think the value education is completely lost.

Useless degrees, or "degrees not in demand," are based on the idea that the only point to anything is generate capital. Is making more money one of the possible benefits of an education, yes. But the claim that we should only be educated on the topics or bodies of knowledge that are of present economic value is: a) not supported by the innovations bore out by history, b) not supported by the ability to live an better life and make better choices that we see in educated populations, and c) relegates the human being to a robot with just enough programing to build widgets.

Firstly, I don't want to live in that kind of world (c). Second, the innovations that come from masses of educated people give rise to entirely new forms. To take a small example, and to root this discussion firmly, let's look at farming. Modern farming is very complex, and that innovation happened with the participation of an increasingly educated group. Crop rotation is based on what each plant needs at the chemical level, and increases the value and productivity of the crop. Synthetic fertilizers are created by harnessing nitrogen in the atmosphere (~70%). Under utilization of the nitrogen cycle creates under performing crops, while over fertilizing can burn the crops. Regulating the amount of water can affect crop yields, as well as surrounding water supplies, which necessarily involves understandings of the basics of geography, geology, and the water cycle as it relates to the natural aquifers and run off. Knowledge about biology and the life cycle of bees help us use the power of pollination effectively, or as is the case currently, ineffectively as seen in the growing Colony Collapse Disorder. This informs buying choices of a host of products and services ranging across entire industries. A well educated farming population could, say, stop buying DDT because they know about biology and chemistry, possibly preventing decades of damage. Skillful use of water resources could see the growth of hydroponic agriculture in dense urban areas, reducing the need for mass transportation, and creating the ability for many more people to experience the value of fresh food. Understanding the basics and even emerging science of nutrition could allow a farmer to plant more dark leafy greens, over planting Iceberg lettuce. Knowledge about virology or disease models could reduce the need for antibiotics, in life stock populations, freeing scientists to work on other problems facing the world, and reducing the growing numbers of ineffective antibiotics in the human population, as seen by the rise of MRSA.

I'm not a huge fan of the monetary system we have going, but since we have it, what do you all think 1 diamond equals in our dollar? 1 Iron?

It's really hard to say. It's practically like real world economy for the fact that there are so many goods and the number of suppliers and producers are changing constantly (depending on who's logged in) and the demand will fluctuate as well. You would almost need a group of people like economists to review it daily and adjust just like a stock market would do.

As far as shop prices go you would have to look at the Admin shop being the "cap" of the market. As in you always have to be lower then them because they have unlimited supply and hoping people would shop at a local business is rather hard to predict because of the convenience of /warp shop being one command away. Honestly though we will always have a need for the admin shop. Some people keep money and users come and go so there has to be a way to introduce new money into the system or else it will dry up eventually.

Here is a problem I foresee in the future for our economy. We have an infinite supply of money, from the adim shop. Eventually that means some players will accumulate vast un-drainable accounts where they could easily play the system. With an infinite influx of money we would normally see massive amounts of inflation over time till Diamonds were 1 million creds or some insane amount merely because people have to much money floating around. The caps on the admin shop do form a pretty solid defense against inflation, but really only for the materials at the shop or related to the ones at the shop. Of course if we take away the admin shop power players will eventually drain the rest of the economy making it hard for new players to participate. So far there isn't anything wrong with the economy. But we do need to have personal responsibility to not take advantage of it.

Sorry, I don't have any data for that.

A lot of figuring out what is worth what is also based on how available it is and how easy it is to obtain. So say you can get yourself ~30 diamond ores (keep in mind this is ores) in an hour of branch mining, then that's $1500 according to that price guide. If you were able to get 5 stacks of leather from a cow farm in the same amount of time, you would think that it should be worth the same as the 30 diamond ores, but it isn't because of supply and demand. Cows are theoretically infinite and a lot easier to find than diamonds. This applies to all mobs and their drops. Mobs like squids, slimes, and others are pretty hard to farm, but it can be done (guardian farms, slime farms [I actually am good at making these], etc...), so their drops will cost more than things like leather and feathers unless there's someone with a farm that is really efficient at it.

tl;dr: Prices on farmable items are the hardest to figure out because there's a theoretical infinite supply.

I've put a lot of thought into the economy over the last few days, and my considered opinion is that the main flaw we have at present is exactly your post.

No one really knows exactly what value to assign to any items, and no one has enough confidence in the system to entrust all their cash to it.

My proposal to mitigate this is simply to make the economy more accessible to all participants, to everyone on the server. There are a few ways we can go about this, and I'm sure my list wont be exhaustive.

1) Tracking the pricing and stock of various chest shops. I don't know if there's a way within the plugin of exporting a list of chest shops with their item name, buy / sell prices, and how much stock the chest has (maybe a snapshot every 24 hours?), but if this is possible, it will enable a lot of clarity as to what people who have already started using the economy think things are worth - and it will bring visibility so that those who are selling for exorbitant prices suddenly have to compete.

2) A central marketplace for all shops on the server. If we were to get agreement from everyone that all shops should be located at one warp in a giant mall type complex, this would also enable easier browsing and more visibility in the economy. Grouping similar themed shops together should enable people to easily shop around and find the right deal for them (example here being something like the bazaars in any RPG where you have a metalworks market, a farm goods market, an ores market, et cetera).

If we make the economy more accessible to our players, then I believe it will massively increase uptake and start to move us off a barter economy where people trade diamonds for iron. Which, so long as the admins keep an eye on things and don't let anyone abuse the system, should only be a good move.
